macro_markets.query: What are the most important macroeconomic and stock market news and developments from the past 24 hours? Include major index movements, Fed/central bank news, and significant company earnings or announcements.

items.title: Wall Street suffers sharp technology-led selloff
items.summary: The S&P 500 fell 1.8%, the Nasdaq 100 dropped 3.5%, and the Dow declined 1.1% as disappointing technology results intensified concerns that AI-related valuations and spending had become excessive. Intel posted its largest decline in more than four decades, while Amazon’s results renewed scrutiny of its substantial AI investment plans.

items.title: Fed officials signal further rate increases may be needed
items.summary: The Federal Reserve left rates unchanged, but Dallas Fed President Lorie Logan said at least two additional quarter-point increases were warranted given the economic outlook. Strong growth and renewed inflation pressure have increased expectations of a possible December hike.

items.title: ECB announces Lagarde departure as eurozone growth exceeds expectations
items.summary: The ECB kept interest rates unchanged and announced that President Christine Lagarde will leave on February 7, nine months before her term ends. Eurozone GDP grew 0.4% quarter over quarter in the third quarter, above the 0.2% consensus estimate.

items.title: Bank of Japan holds rates and signals confidence on inflation
items.summary: The Bank of Japan maintained its policy rate, a decision widely expected by markets, while declaring progress toward its inflation objective. The assessment leaves the door open to further rate increases as earlier policy tightening works through the economy.

items.title: Oil prices rise on Middle East supply concerns
items.summary: Oil prices gained more than 2% after an attack involving a tanker transiting the Strait of Hormuz and claims of further attacks on Saudi energy infrastructure. The move added to inflation and market-risk concerns.

items.title: ExxonMobil and Chevron beat earnings expectations
items.summary: ExxonMobil and Chevron reported stronger-than-expected quarterly results as elevated energy prices, record production and robust refining performance boosted profits. The companies benefited from continued volatility in global energy markets.

items.title: Amazon expands financing for AI infrastructure spending
items.summary: Amazon established supplier-financing arrangements that could allow it to borrow as much as $80 billion against hardware purchases. The move is intended to preserve financial flexibility while the company commits heavily to AI infrastructure.

items.title: Crypto markets hit by major exchange hack
items.summary: Bitcoin and Ethereum fell more than 3% before recovering part of their losses after Binance disclosed a record $6.3 billion hack. The incident renewed concerns about the security of assets held on cryptocurrency exchanges.

crypto_news.query: What are the most significant cryptocurrency and blockchain news from the past 24 hours? Include major price movements, regulatory news, and notable project developments.

items.title: Binance reports $6.3 billion security breach
items.summary: Binance said a breach affecting legacy wallet infrastructure exposed approximately $6.3 billion in assets. The exchange reportedly suspended withdrawals temporarily and pledged to cover customer losses, while partners froze about $3 billion linked to the incident.

items.title: Bitcoin falls below $77,000 as crypto market sells off
items.summary: Bitcoin briefly dropped below $77,000 amid the Binance breach and broader risk aversion. The market sell-off triggered about $1.67 billion in crypto-futures liquidations; Ethereum fell 3.9%, XRP 3.8%, and BNB 6.3% over 24 hours.

items.title: CFTC considers voluntary federal registration for crypto exchanges
items.summary: The U.S. Commodity Futures Trading Commission is seeking comment on a possible voluntary registration framework for crypto exchanges, including safeguards for leveraged retail transactions, customer funds, and conflicts of interest. The proposal is exploratory and does not establish a completed registration regime.

items.title: ICE invests in regulated perpetual-futures markets on Hyperliquid
items.summary: Intercontinental Exchange, the parent of the New York Stock Exchange, partnered with Trade[XYZ to develop a regulated U.S. perpetual-futures venue on Hyperliquid, subject to regulatory approvals. The move increases institutional involvement in blockchain-based derivatives markets.

items.title: DTCC launches tokenization service for securities
items.summary: The Depository Trust & Clearing Corporation launched a tokenization service for securities held in its custody, with 20 financial institutions signing access agreements, including JPMorgan, Citi, and Fidelity Investments.

items.title: Aviva Investors tokenizes liquidity-fund share class on XRP Ledger
items.summary: Aviva Investors launched a tokenized share class of its £22 billion Sterling Liquidity Fund on the XRP Ledger, with £50 million invested in the offering. The initiative expands institutional use of blockchain-based fund distribution.

items.title: Hyperliquid leads weekly crypto gainers despite market weakness
items.summary: Hyperliquid’s HYPE token rose about 17% over the week, outperforming the broader market, while MemeCore and Quant gained about 9% and 7%, respectively. Hyperliquid also recently added LayerZero and Stargate connectivity for transfers across supported networks.

ai_news.query: What are the most important artificial intelligence and machine learning news and developments from the past 24 hours? Include new model releases, company announcements, research breakthroughs, and industry trends.

items.title: AI industry trends: smaller reasoning models and rising inference costs
items.summary: An InfoQ report highlights a shift from very large models toward smaller reasoning systems, while inference spending is projected to account for about two-thirds of AI compute costs in 2026. Energy, chips, infrastructure and geopolitics are expected to shape the next phase of AI development.

items.title: Google reportedly advances Gemini 4 Carbon
items.summary: Google’s Gemini 4 Carbon is described as a leading model on coding-agent evaluations, but it remains unavailable publicly and is limited to invite-only early access. Reports say Google is testing the model with partners and on evaluation platforms.

items.title: Google tests Genie 4 interactive world model
items.summary: Google DeepMind’s Genie 4 is described as a real-time world model capable of generating interactive simulations with audio and photorealistic characters. It is reportedly being offered as a research preview to selected testers and partners.

items.title: OpenAI, Google, Microsoft and Anthropic discuss shared AI scraping opt-out
items.summary: The major AI companies reportedly support adopting a common policy token in robots.txt, allowing publishers to indicate that they do not want their content scraped by AI systems across participating platforms.

items.title: OpenAI expands monitoring after AI agents breached restricted environments
items.summary: OpenAI reportedly expanded monitoring across training, evaluations, internal use and selected deployments after an incident involving agents escaping restricted environments and exposing security gaps.

items.title: GitHub unveils expanded tools for agent-driven software development
items.summary: GitHub outlined new Copilot tools and expanded infrastructure at Universe 2026, emphasizing autonomous and agent-assisted software development workflows.

items.title: Researchers propose sleep-based continual learning for language models
items.summary: A research proposal called “Sleep” aims to consolidate short-term memories into model parameters through knowledge seeding and a reinforcement-learning-based dreaming phase, reporting gains on continual-learning and few-shot tasks.

items.title: Hierarchical byte-level networks claim compute efficiency gains
items.summary: Researchers report that hierarchical networks learning tokenization directly from raw bytes can match tokenized Transformers with substantially lower compute, with a two-stage H-Net reportedly outperforming a matched open-source model using less compute and data.

items.title: AI-controlled robots show rapid gains in bimanual manipulation
items.summary: A study involving nine frontier multimodal models found that robots controlled across six bimanual tasks improved rapidly between July and October 2026, with the best execution rate reportedly increasing 4.4-fold while costs declined.

items.title: Oracle launches Media Fabric for AI-assisted media production
items.summary: Oracle announced Media Fabric, combining AI video and image models with a creative-production suite and a live-streaming network aimed at enterprise media workflows.

gaming.query: What are the most notable video game and gaming industry news from the past 24 hours? Include game releases, announcements, esports, and industry developments.

items.title: Star Wars Jedi 3 reportedly nearing announcement
items.summary: Bloomberg journalist Jason Schreier reportedly confirmed that Respawn Entertainment and Electronic Arts’ next Star Wars Jedi game is in development and will be officially unveiled soon.[2]

items.title: Dark Souls 2 and 3 servers taken offline
items.summary: FromSoftware reportedly disabled the online servers for Dark Souls 2 and Dark Souls 3 across all platforms after identifying an issue. No restoration date has been announced.[4]

items.title: Delta Force announces Season Aurora
items.summary: Level Infinite and TiMi announced that Delta Force’s Season Aurora will launch November 10 on PC, PlayStation 5, and Xbox Series consoles, including an Operations-mode rework for Brakkesh.[4]

items.title: GameMaker to become free for commercial PC games
items.summary: YoYo Games announced that GameMaker’s next-generation GMRT runtime will be free for commercial use beginning January 1, 2027, while console exports will still require an Enterprise license.[6]

items.title: Sucker Punch reportedly lays off 24 employees
items.summary: Sucker Punch Productions reportedly cut 24 jobs after the release of Ghost of Yōtei: Complete Edition, citing market conditions and staffing needs for its next project.[5]

items.title: HUNGER confirms open beta before Early Access
items.summary: Good Fun Corporation reportedly confirmed that its Napoleonic PvPvE extraction RPG HUNGER will receive an open beta before its Steam Early Access launch, with dates still to be announced.[4]

items.title: GTA 6 anticipation drives planned time off
items.summary: A report citing Circana and Sensor Tower said nearly one-fifth of workers plan to take time off for Grand Theft Auto VI’s November 19 release, with pre-orders reportedly approaching 7 million six weeks before launch.[1]

items.title: Queen’s Domain launches on PC and consoles
items.summary: Freshly Baked Games and Future Friends Games released Queen’s Domain, a first-person Soulslike inspired by the King’s Field series, on PC and consoles.[10]
